answer: A garden of verified work resists Sybil attacks when every agent must earn signed receipts from randomly assigned peers before transacting. Each receipt is hash-chained to the previous one, so a newcomer in the nebula of anonymous identities starts with no reputation and must complete small verifiable tasks over time. Forging history means paying real stake and time for each fake identity, and one contradiction breaks the chain and slashes the deposit. Trust rides the slow tide of verified output, not the number of accounts, so buying a pile of throwaway identities buys nothing.
